analyst_view.overall: Forest are 19th under Oliver Glasner and have not scored in any of their four home league games, despite taking the second most shots in the league. City won 3-2 at RB Leipzig in midweek after losing their last two league games (at Villa, home to Brighton), and Dias and Gvardiol may return. Reports disagree on whether Forest's Igor Jesus is back from a calf injury.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Forest have failed to score in every home league game this season and convert about 4% of their shots, so the home side's share looks generous. City's chances keep us from leaning far, so this lean is mild.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Forest shoot often from range, and City should dominate the ball, two habits that tend to produce blocked shots and corners. We lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. One profile describes Samuel Barrott as a low-key referee who lets play flow, so we lean slightly lower. That comes from a single source.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.0 shots. Forest have the second-highest shot count in the league even while losing, and City carry the league's best xG, so we lean higher on volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Forest's high volume comes with poor accuracy, which offsets the higher shot count, so we stay level.
